runs.text: A program can fail in three ways, and the most dangerous one gives no warning at all.
The problem
Your classmate wrote three versions of the tip calculator. The engine does not even accept the first one. The second works until someone types
0 friends
. The third always shows a number, but with a bill of
and
4 friends
it says each one pays
What is wrong with each one, and how would you have found out?
Try it
Read the three versions shown further down, under
Write
, before running them. Note what you suspect about each one.
The first is missing a semicolon at the end of a line. The second divides by the number of friends, and dividing by 0 has no answer. The third computes only the tip,
, and forgot to add the bill: 12 divided by 4 gives 3.
Understand
What is asked is not a new program. It is to classify the failures and find a way to discover them before someone else does.
Plan
For each version, three questions in order:

entries.text: Does it finish, or does it stop on the way?
Does what it shows match the worked example?

runs.text: The new tool
Each question of the plan uncovers a different kind of failure.

entries.text: is a text the engine cannot understand: the program never gets to start.
appears on the way: the program starts, but stops at an instruction it cannot carry out.
stops nothing: the program finishes and shows a wrong result. The engine cannot see it, because it did exactly what the text says.

blocks.description: A bus trip from departure to destination. Step 1: the bus does not start, like a compile error, which the engine reports before starting. Step 2: the bus breaks down on the way, like a runtime error, which the engine reports when it happens. Step 3: the bus arrives in another town, like a logic error, which only your test cases reveal.

caption.text: The engine reports the first two. Only you discover the third one, by comparing with your examples.

runs.text: The bus does not start: a compile error. The engine reports it before starting.
The bus breaks down on the way: a runtime error. The engine reports it when it happens.
The bus arrives, but in another town: a logic error. Nobody warns you.
When the engine finds an error, it writes a
diagnostic
: it says where the problem is (line and column), with a code and a message.

figure.description: At the top, the diagnostic as data: code incompatibleTypesInAssignment, semantic class and error severity, span on line 2 and arguments expected Integer and found String. An arrow with the language template leads to the presented message.

caption.text: The same diagnostic seen as data and as a message. The message is built with a template in the interface language and the arguments.

runs.text: Write
There is no new solution: the three versions are run.

blocks.title: Version A

diagnostics.message: Expected a semicolon at the end of the statement

runs.text: The diagnostic points at line 6, where the semicolon is missing, and the program never gets to ask anything.

blocks.title: Version B, with 0 friends

runs.text: Version B starts well: it asks for both values. It stops at the last instruction, when dividing by 0.

blocks.title: Version C
blocks.output:
¿Cuánto es la cuenta?
¿Cuántos amigos pagan?
Cada uno paga: 3

runs.text: Version C finishes without complaining. If you did not have the worked example (33), you would accept the 3.
Test
A
test case
is an input with the output you expect, taken from a worked example. Choosing them well is a craft: the most useful ones are the
edge cases
, which sit right on the limit where a hasty program gets it wrong.

blocks.description: A number line with the number of friends from -1 to 5, split into three zones: odd for 0 and negatives, edge at 1, and normal from 2 upwards. One point is marked in each zone: 0, 1 and 4.

caption.text: One case from each zone: the normal one uncovers logic errors; the edge and the odd one, those waiting at the borders.

runs.text: The normal case uncovers version C. The odd one uncovers B, and C too.
Improve
In one sentence:
Before accepting a program, I test it with a normal case, an edge case and an odd one, and compare with my worked examples
The odd case has no fix yet: to warn
nobody is paying
instead of stopping, the program would have to decide. It stays open.
What you learned

points.text: A compile error stops the program from starting; a runtime error stops it on the way; a logic error gives a wrong result without warning.
A diagnostic says where the problem is, with a code and a message.
A test case is an input with its expected output; an edge case sits right on the limit where a hasty program gets it wrong.

runs.text: Practise

entries.text: Version C compiles and finishes. Ask them to test it before showing the worked example.
«The error is on the line the engine points at».
Sometimes it is just before: in version A, the semicolon is missing at the end of line 6.
Testing only with the example in the statement.
Always ask for an edge case and an odd one.

runs.text: Until now every program always does the same thing. What if, depending on the data, it has to do different things, such as warning that you cannot divide among 0 friends?
